title: Coin Change
prompt:
You have coins of the given denominations, with an unlimited supply of each. Return the fewest coins that add up exactly to amount, or -1 if it cannot be done.

Write coinChange(coins, amount).

coinChange([1, 2, 5], 11);   // 3   (5 + 5 + 1)
coinChange([2], 3);          // -1
coinChange([1], 0);          // 0   (zero coins make zero)
coinChange([1, 3, 4], 6);    // 2   (3 + 3; "biggest coin first" would give 4 + 1 + 1 = 3 coins)

Constraints: 1 to 12 coin types, each between 1 and 500; amount between 0 and 10,000.

tests.name: greedy (biggest coin first) is wrong here
larger amount (needs the table, not plain recursion)

hints: Trigger: "fewest coins" / "minimum number of ..." to reach a total, with unlimited reuse. Greedy (largest coin first) looks right but fails on coins like [1,3,4]. Min over choices that repeat is DP.

Idea: fewest(a) = fewest coins for amount a. Whatever the best solution is, it has some last coin c, and the rest makes a - c as cheaply as possible. So fewest(a) = 1 + min over coins c of fewest(a - c), with fewest(0) = 0.

Code shape: const fewest = new Array(amount + 1).fill(Infinity); fewest[0] = 0; for (let a = 1; a <= amount; a++) for (const coin of coins) if (coin <= a) fewest[a] = Math.min(fewest[a], fewest[a - coin] + 1); then return -1 if it is still Infinity.
explain:
Time O(amount × number of coins), space O(amount). For amount 1,000 and 4 coins that is 4,000 steps; the plain recursion would branch 4 ways at every level.

Say it: "Greedy fails on coins like 1, 3, 4, so I'll use DP. Let fewest of a be the minimum coins for amount a; the best answer ends with some coin c, so fewest of a is 1 plus the minimum of fewest of a minus c. I fill the table from 0 up to the amount: O(amount times coins) time, O(amount) space."
